title: RFE: ~Independently-maintained AdditionalImageStores
body:
### Feature request description

Usage of AdditionalImageStores as layer store for RWStorage could lead to broken RWStorage (at least in overlay driver) if any of the stores in AdditionalImageStores alters.

In case an image is pulled into RWStorage which has layers already existing in ROStorage a link is made from RWStorage to ROStorage instead of pulling layer. If in anytime in future the ROStorage alters so that the link breaks the RWStorage becomes corrupted.



### Suggest potential solution

Obviously the behavior is useful generally in many cases but it is problematic in others. Therefore the decision should be left to the clients to define which AdditionalImageStores can be used as well as layer store for RWStorage.
The suggestion is to mark the stores in storage.conf so that they can optionally be ignored as layer-store.

comments.body:
> Obviously the behavior is useful generally in many cases but it is problematic in others. Therefore the decision should be left to the clients to define which AdditionalImageStores can be used as well as layer store for RWStorage.
> The suggestion is to mark the stores in storage.conf so that they can optionally be ignored as layer-store.

in what cases would it be useful to leave these stores in the `storage.conf` file but ignore them?

@giuseppe thanks for the reply.

My suggestion does not entail ignoring addtionalImagesStores entries as image storage rather ignore them as layer store to deduplicate layers of RW storage. So that clients can still start containers off of both image-stores (RO/RW) but still the possibility to update the stores independent of each other maintained without risk of breaking links.

If I understand correctly, the effect would be to two separate, _independently maintained_, stores, each of which can add or remove images together with their dependent layers, such that removing an image, and its associated layers, from one store, does not break anything in the other store, because no layers are shared/reused _across_ stores.

And that would also mean that putting shared base images to the additional store would have no benefit; a pull of an application derived from that base image would need to write the full image into the local store. IOW, that additional store would only be useful for hosting/distributing complete top-level applications (which is still useful, sure).

That’s not a trivial “do not check the other store” boolean: if an image is pulled into the local store, we would need to make sure that _all_ layers are stored into the local store. Right now, layer/image existence is a yes/no state; from e.g. Podman’s view, a layer either exists (and is always reused), or doesn’t. We would need some new state indicating “a layer exists but pull it anyway, or at least copy-up from the other store”. 

That’s… a plausible feature in principle. My initial impression is that we already have way too many options and knobs (additional image stores, additional layer stores, transient stores, …?) with unclear interactions, and in some cases likely-rarely-used, possibly unmaintained, or outright dubious, implementations (_just the top level_ of `drivers/overlay.Driver.get` is 411 lines!), that I’m intuitively very reluctant to add to the complexity. But I would _probably_ not be doing that work or maintaining the code…

Following your line of thoughts @mtrmac on how many configuration are around the storage sharing and how  interactions are unclear, I can see how defining the scope of each feature may help to keep knobs a bit saner. 
Now to put this into perspective of this feature request I see it beneficial how additional image stores should **not** necessary mean additional layer store to differentiate between layer and image. 
Such that if the same set of image stores required for layer stores, it should be specified so instead of implicitly assuming so. In this manner those two terms would present a better name<->scope association.

This now affects bootc systems with physically bound images (e.g. MicroShift at the edge): the images are embedded in an additional store under /usr, every OS update replaces that store, and pulled images that shared its layers break. Reproducer: https://github.com/vrothberg/physically-bound-image-reproducer (Red Hat tracks it as RHEL-75827). The current workaround is copying every embedded image into the main store at boot.

I have a prototype of the “copy instead of reuse” state @mtrmac described: an opt-in pull_options key, and in commitLayer a layer from a read-only store is copied into the primary store under a different ID instead of being reused. The contents still come from the local store, so nothing is downloaded; only the disk space is paid twice. The ID has to differ because overlay would otherwise resolve it to the additional store’s directory. It’s about 25 lines in containers/image, plus a test. https://github.com/yuvaldekel/container-libs/tree/isolate-additional-image-stores

Would a PR along these lines be welcome? Should it be per store rather than global?
please share first the configuration change.  How would it look?  And yes, it should be per-store

Thanks. I'd mark it on the store path, the same way `additionallayerstores` uses `:ref`:

```toml
[storage.options]
additionalimagestores = [
  "/usr/lib/containers/storage:isolated",
  "/mnt/shared/storage",
]
```

Layers from an `isolated` store are copied into the primary store (from local disk, under a different layer ID) instead of being reused. Stores without the suffix work the same as today.
`additionalimagestores` takes no options today, so this is new syntax. With overlay, an older version fails on the suffixed path instead of silently ignoring it.

Does that look good, and is `isolated` a good name?
"copy" sounds good. Should I implement it that way and open a PR?
I am fine with it, we could wait a bit longer to gain feedback from others too

Looking at the commit in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/compare/main...yuvaldekel:container-libs:isolate-additional-image-stores
- with the design that pre-existing layers in the RO stores are copied, not re-pulled, fine, a local change around `commitLayer` makes sense.
- If the configuration should be per-store, the existing `layer.ReadOnly` check will need redesigning in _some_ way.
- Nothing guarantees that a `additionalImageStoreCopyLayerID`-named layer does not exist in one of the read-only stores already. At the same time, if we don’t make layer IDs deterministic, we break sharing of parent layers, so just making the layer IDs random would not be sufficient. In _principle_, I think duplicate layer IDs across the stores _should_ be possible and _should_ work fine, but how easy it would be to create such a layer, given existing stores, is another matter.

---

Looking at the proposed config: I strongly oppose adding syntax to strings. It does not scale to adding more options, it gives up on parsing/formatting tools for the config file format, and it breaks legitimate inputs (paths with `:`, in this case).

We could always add a new field, maybe just `additional_image_stores` (with underscores this time) which is an array of typed structures, and support both formats (rejecting configs that use both fields).

Thanks, that makes sense — I'll drop the suffix. Something like this?

```toml
[[storage.options.additional_image_stores]]
path = "/usr/lib/containers/storage"
copy_layers = true
```

Rejecting a config that sets both fields sounds good. For drop-in files: should a later file replace the `additional_image_stores` list, or should it support appending like `additionalimagestores` does with `{append = true}`?

On the IDs: the loop in `commitLayer` already derives the copy ID again if it also exists in a read-only store, so it stays deterministic. I first tried keeping the same ID, but overlay's `create` resolves the ID through `dir2` to the additional store's directory and tries to remove it. Would you prefer changing the drivers to create only in their own home, so copies keep the original ID?

Uh, drop-ins… I forgot about those. I don’t immediately know. I suppose we should not be losing features that exist today.

Really, as I’m sure you have sen, all of the AIS code is inconsistently weaving across 3 layers of abstraction in c/storage, and in many ways an attempt to do one small thing cleanly would trigger the need for a large-scale redesign. And _not_ doing that small thing cleanly makes things worse for the future.

I'd like to try doing it properly, in small steps. Looking at the code, `imagestore` (the writable one) already goes through typed fields: `StoreOptions.ImageStore` → the store → `graphdriver.Options.ImageStore`. Additional image stores instead become `imagestore=` driver option strings, each driver parses them, and the store asks the driver for the list back.

As a first step, with no behaviour change, I'd make additional image stores follow the same path as `ImageStore`:

- a typed list in `StoreOptions`, filled from the config
- the store builds its read-only stores from that list, not from `graphDriver.AdditionalImageStores()`
- drivers get the paths through `graphdriver.Options`

`overlay.imagestore=` passed as a driver option (`--storage-opt`, `STORAGE_OPTS`) would still need to work. I see two ways: the store picks those up and merges them into its list, or the drivers keep parsing them and the store merges in `graphDriver.AdditionalImageStores()` (those can't carry per-store settings anyway). Which would you prefer, or is there a better place?

After that, the new `additional_image_stores` config field (with append for drop-ins), and then the per-store copy setting.

Does this look like the right first step?
Last I heard the plan for bootc was to rely on #651 to deduplicate. Is AIS still an essential part of the plan?

I'm not sure. I'm coming at this as a bootc user on RHEL 9 image mode, where physically bound images are shipped as an additional image store under `/usr`, and RHEL-75827 is open about exactly this breakage (the workaround there is a `dir:` copy into the main store at boot). I don't know whether bootc there uses #651 yet, or when it would.

As I understand #651, it lets bootc build its deployment from an image in containers-storage without storing it twice. I don't see yet how that covers application images that have to be on a node before it ever reaches a registry; today that's what embedding them in the OS image under `/usr` solves. If bootc has a plan for that which doesn't use an additional image store, I agree a redesign just for this isn't worth it.

If AIS is still expected to be used for this, I'm still willing to do the steps above.
